items.title: Our system
items.why: Our system: class-aware shards with one class per slice, replay of earlier classes, and a learned gate that is retrained on every deletion. Built once, then each of the 10 classes is deleted in turn while time-to-compliance (TTC) and accuracy are measured.

items.title: Single-model baseline
items.why: Gold standard: one ResNet-20 retrained from scratch without the class. Exact by definition; it sets the time and accuracy every other system is compared with.

items.title: Inference benchmark
items.why: Inference latency and throughput of every system on the M5 Pro.

items.title: Original paper reproduction
items.why: Runs the ORIGINAL paper's code on this Mac (shards x slices, deleting 'dog') with nothing else on the GPU, so the original timings can be checked fairly.

items.title: Our system, stale gate
items.why: Negative control: keeps the OLD gate, which still learned from the deleted class. Shows that accuracy checks cannot detect this; only the lineage audit can, so the gate must be retrained.

items.title: Availability test
items.why: What the system can still serve, compliantly, while a deletion rebuild is running.

items.title: Prediction backfill
items.why: Housekeeping: adds saved test-set predictions to earlier results (no training).

items.title: ARCANE baseline
items.why: ARCANE (Yan et al., IJCAI 2022), the closest prior method: one one-class model per class. A competing BASELINE we re-implemented (no official code), not a reproduction of our own paper.

items.title: SISA baseline
items.why: Classic SISA (Bourtoule et al. 2021) with random sharding. Every shard holds every class, so deleting one class retrains all shards: the baseline our class-aware placement improves on.

items.title: ARCANE baseline
items.why: ARCANE again without BatchNorm: a fix for its one-class models collapsing, so the baseline gets its fairest chance.

items.title: Scratch reference
items.why: Exactness check on the GPU: two independent from-scratch builds without one class. The unlearned system must be no further from them than they are from each other (GPU noise floor).

Phase 0.label: Setup
Phase 0.about: Environment, data, code repositories, GPU throughput benchmark.

Phase 1.label: Reproduction & exactness
Phase 1.about: Re-run the original code, audit its evaluation, and re-implement the core so that deletion is EXACT by construction (proven bit-for-bit on CPU).

Phase 2.label: Systems evaluation
Phase 2.about: Our system vs SISA, ARCANE and full retraining on all 10 classes x 3 seeds: time-to-compliance, storage, latency, verification, sequential deletions, design space.

Phase 3.label: Evidence review
Phase 3.about: Decide the paper's claims and title from the measured results.

Phase 4.label: Paper
Phase 4.about: Write the paper from the results files (tables generated by script), audit references, compile, final push.

project.title: Erasure-ready class unlearning
project.about: We are rebuilding our class-unlearning paper as a systems paper: a classifier that can forget an entire class on request, exactly (as if it had never been trained on it), with measured time-to-compliance, storage and verification. The Mac trains in overnight shifts; Claude Code runs the experiments and writes the analysis.
project.hardware: Apple M5 Pro, 24 GB, PyTorch on the Metal GPU (MPS)
